newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PLDT sheds 2.32 pct, tracking Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: PLDT sheds 2.32 pct, tracking Wall Street.

text.p: Telecommunications giant Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co slipped 35 pesos, or 2.32 percent, to 1,470 in early morning trade on Friday, taking its cue from the overnight fall of its American Depositary Receipts (ADR), brokers said.

"PLDT is just following the drop of its ADR in Wall Street. Sentiment is also negative on the issue because of its...(lower than expected) first quarter profits," said Bernard Gorospe, analyst at Citisecurities Inc.
PLDT had reached a low of 1,450 pesos early in the session.
"People are still disappointed with the first quarter earnings of the company," said Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor-Hagedorn Securities.
PLDT reported on Monday a 1.8 percent drop in its profits for the first quarter of the year to 1.28 billion pesos, which it attributed to the cost of a redundancy programme.
PLDT was the third most actively traded stock in the early session with turnover of 566.40 million pesos.
